subject: Aligning POC workshop timing, prompt inventory, and output schema

Subject: POC workshop: prompts, routing and a short load window

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team found the throughput examples helpful. We want to move to a short hands-on POC so we can validate prompt behavior and routing under realistic traffic. High-level ask: a half-day, hands-on session where we review our prompt inventory, confirm structured-output requirements, and run two short load windows (routing + KV-cache behavior).

Can you share availability for the week of Nov 29–Dec 3? Prefer mornings PT. Also: a couple of questions to help prep the session —
- Do you have a prompt inventory template we should fill out ahead of time?
- For structured output, what format constraints do you typically validate (JSON schema, strict keys, enumerations)?
- For the load window: what TPS targets are realistic for a starter run on Dedicated vs Hosted?

Looping in procurement once we lock a date, there may be a short paperwork step.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this to a tighter plan.

Best,
Aria Simmons
Director of AI Platforms | Acme Health
aria@acmehealth.com

Subject: Re: POC workshop: prompts, routing and a short load window

Hi Aria —

Thanks for the clear ask. Nov 29–Dec 3 works; proposed windows (PT mornings) below — please pick one preferred slot and we will send a calendar invite:

- Tue Nov 30, 9:30–13:00 PT — half-day (recommended)
- Wed Dec 1, 08:30–12:00 PT — earlier start
- Thu Dec 2, 10:00–13:30 PT — later morning

Quick answers to your prep questions:
- Prompt inventory: Im attaching a short template we use (columns for prompt name, intent, examples, expected structured fields, rejection criteria). Please fill what you can; we can always iterate during the session.
- Structured output: we typically validate against a JSON schema for the main payload plus a lightweight enum for status codes; where possible we ask for sample ground-truth outputs so we can align parsing and safety rules.
- Load window targets: for an initial routing + KV-cache run we recommend targeting 15–25 TPS on Hosted to exercise batching and routing; Dedicated can comfortably hit 50+ TPS depending on model size and quantization profile. We will scope the exact targets once we see your prompt length distribution.

Ben will own load-run orchestration and Olga will cover routing/fallback policy setup. I attached a short Proposed-POC-Agenda PDF to give a sense of timing.

If that all looks good Ill slot you for Wed Dec 1 (08:30–12:00 PT) tentatively and share the invite + pre-POC checklist.

Cheers,
Markus Klein
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai
